problem: Graph-only retrieval (VL-KnG) captures object relations but underrepresents broader temporal continuity and context, so it degrades on questions needing evidence aggregated across multiple non-cooccurring moments in long egocentric trajectories. Full-context VLMs handle this but are slow and must reprocess the video for every query.
motivation: Robots accumulate long egocentric navigation trajectories and later need to answer retrospective questions (where was X, which area was visited first) grounded in visual evidence. A persistent, precomputed, queryable memory is needed that supports both relational reasoning and temporal/contextual retrieval, with efficient repeated querying.
key_idea: Combine a VL-KnG spatio-temporal knowledge graph with a persistent segment-level caption+multimodal-embedding memory, retrieve from both in parallel, and fuse them in an LLM reasoner that outputs flat or grouped ranked evidence frames and an answer.
insight: The two memories are complementary: the graph gives object/relational localization, while segment memory adds temporal context. Per-category gains are largest on temporal-global and temporally scattered aggregation (Temp. Scatt. MRR@1 0.55 vs 0.28/0.32 for VL-KnG; Temp. Global 0.72 vs 0.42/0.41), while graph-only methods remain competitive on object search and action-place. Ablations show balanced 0.5/0.5 text-visual fusion is best (visual-dominated weighting degrades), and object-centric query rewriting improves Top-3/5 retrieval but lowers answer accuracy.
method: Segmentation and captioning: the trajectory is split into ~2 s segments (5 fps video), and a VLM writes constrained object-centric captions (attributes, readable text, a fixed spatial-relation vocabulary).
Segment-level memory: each segment stores an ID, its caption, a text embedding (text-embedding-3-large) and a visual embedding (ViCLIP), following VideoAgent-style memory.
Spatio-temporal knowledge graph: an LLM extracts objects, attributes and relations from caption chunks, and VL-KnG's STOA links repeated objects across chunks into a global graph.

Hybrid retrieval: the question is rewritten into an object-centric query and matched against segment memory with fused score 0.5*vis+0.5*text; in parallel the graph is queried GraphRAG-style for segment-anchored subgraphs.
Frame-level grounding: retrieved segments are mapped to sparsely sampled frames (every 60th frame, plus at least one frame from each evidence interval).
Joint reasoning and ranking: an LLM reads caption evidence and graph evidence together and outputs a flat ranked frame list or grouped frame lists (one per temporal moment), plus the answer.

setting.backbone: VLM for captioning plus LLM for graph extraction and reasoning (specific models not named in the text); ViCLIP and text-embedding-3-large for embeddings
setting.observation: monocular RGB egocentric video (5 fps), processed offline
setting.action_space: not applicable (video QA and evidence retrieval, no actions)
setting.simulator: none (real EgoWalk trajectories, indoor and outdoor)

numbers.extra: 8 trajectories, 262 questions; frame decimation every 60th frame; w_vis=w_text=0.5, k_KG=k_mem=10

numbers_note: Split names are not given by the paper; 'test' is used as a placeholder for the whole benchmark. Per-category results and ablations use subsets (two trajectories, 84 questions).
results: On WalkieKnowledgeT+, VL-MemKnG lifts Retrieval Acc@1 from 58.33 to 66.83 and Recall@1 from 34.50 to 40.55 over the best VL-KnG variant. It is also best at Top-1 among all methods, marginally above Gemini 2.5 Pro (66.03 Acc@1, 40.50 Recall@1). Gemini 2.5 Pro and Qwen 3.5+ remain better at k=3/5 and in answer accuracy (Qwen 70.59 vs 65.81). Query latency is 1.28 s vs 5.62 s (Gemini Flash), 27.78 s (Pro) and 45.37 s (Qwen 3.5+), with token break-even after about 20 queries.
limitations: Depends on caption quality from the underlying VLM; caption errors propagate to both memories.
The knowledge graph is built offline with no incremental updates, so it does not support streaming settings.
Small benchmark (8 trajectories, 262 questions); ablations use only two trajectories. Full-context VLMs still lead at larger k and in answer accuracy.
